newsitem.title: USA: Turkey faulted for worsening rights record.
newsitem.headline: Turkey faulted for worsening rights record.

text.p: Turkey had serious human rights problems in 1996 and its record deteriorated in some respects, the United States said on Thursday.

"The government was unable to sustain improvements made in 1995 and, as a result, its record was uneven in 1996 and deteriorated in some respects," the State Department said in its annual report on human rights worldwide, adding: "Serious human rights problems continued."

The report said of "particular concern" was the situation in southeast Turkey, where the government "has long denied its Kurdish population, located largely in the southeast, basic cultural and linguistic rights."

The report accused Ankara of forcibly displacing an estimated 560,000 noncombatants in its campaign against the Kurdistan Worker's Party, a separatist movement known as the PKK, which the United States and Turkey call a terrorist group.
The report said that Ankara's efforts to compensate the people inside Turkey "remained inadequate."

Also, the United States charged that "extrajudicial killings, including deaths in detention, from the excessive use of force, in safe house raids, and mystery killings continued to occur with disturbing frequency."
